correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary Boolean relation A⊆X×Y, rectangle truth means some U∈F,V∈G satisfy U×V⊆A; first iterated truth is H={x:A_x∈G}∈F. Rectangle→both iterates follows from upward closure. If every minimal F member is a singleton, choose x in H whose singleton lies in F and use its G-good row as V. If G is principal with minimal V0, then H×V0 is a rectangle. Conversely choose minimal U∈F of size≥2 and distinct incomparable minimal G neighborhoods V0,V1, assign row V0 at one u, V1 at other u∈U, empty elsewhere. Iterated box holds but any F rectangle requires all of U and an admissible subset of V0∩V1, impossible by minimality. Symmetric criterion follows. Counting proper families via Dedekind antichains T_n=D_n−2, singleton-generated/principal each q_n=2^n−1 with n-class overlap, inclusion–exclusion yields both given census formulas. Independently enumerated all 18 local families on each three-point carrier and every 512 Boolean valuation for 324 pairs: 203 first converse, 131 both, and all 165888 tests agreed. Unlimited finite carrier result follows from the analytic minimal-neighborhood proof, not finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Nonempty finite carriers and proper upward-closed neighborhood families excluding empty set only.
Result does not claim infinite filters, arbitrary modal completeness or global frame census.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact classification of local converse mixing in a natural nonnormal product semantics, with a sharp 3×3 onset of both failures and a whole closed enumerative census. The structure matters for whether a third modality collapses to two iterated modalities; the counts provide independently useful exact model frequencies. It is not a trivial rephrasing of finite principal filters because their nonnormal complements are the decisive new cases.
